scope: Derived quantitative influence and actual reversible Gibbs update contraction for arbitrary finite local factors. A weighted support-size budget alpha and a current-support independent coloring with C colors give the rate 1-(1-alpha)/C; alpha<1 makes it strict. Exact elimination supplies recursively computed oscillation bounds for every generated factor. The actual SU(2) Wilson tower is identified with this construction; its seed budget is at most 36*beta and each first-step generated factor receives the conservative weight at most 48*beta. No cutoff-uniform entry into alpha<1, physical-transfer contraction, continuum limit or mass gap is proved.

quantitative_results.hypotheses: Finite compact-spin Gibbs system with continuous actual factors Phi_p supported on D_p and oscillation at most w_p>=0.
quantitative_results.influence: For i!=j, c_ij=(1/2)*sum_{p:i,j in D_p} w_p; c_ii=0. Actual conditional expectations of a test of oscillation d differ by at most c_ij*d.
quantitative_results.budget: sum_j c_ij = (1/2)*sum_{p:i in D_p} (card(D_p erase i))*w_p.
quantitative_results.mixing: A coloring independent for the current factor supports, with C colors, and every row budget <=alpha yields auxiliary L2 norm contraction <=[1-(1-alpha)/C]. For alpha<1 this is strict; the rate is volume-uniform only when alpha and C are uniformly controlled.
quantitative_results.elimination: Retained factors keep their old weights. A generated factor for an eliminated site i receives weight 2*sum_{p:i in D_p} w_p. The oscillation bound is proved for the literal negative-log-integral factor and iterated through the actual factor construction.
quantitative_results.wilson: For beta>=0, seed plaquette weight 4*beta; initial row budget <=36*beta; first generated-factor weight <=48*beta. For admissible elimination schedules the represented law equals the exact Wilson induced Gibbs law.
quantitative_results.mixed_criterion: If the full action mixed rectangles are bounded by r(i,j)>=0 and each row sum is <=4*alpha, the actual influence is <=r(i,j)/4 and the same L2 contraction follows. Factorwise rectangle bounds are proved to add to the full bound. Whole-factor smallness is not required. Uniform bounds for the actual physical Wilson trajectory remain unproved.

attack_outcome.completed: A proved quantitative mixing criterion for general generated local interactions, with an actual-kernel identity, L2 contraction, computed integration bounds and explicit Wilson specialization. A sharper mixed-rectangle criterion connects the existing free-energy rectangle estimates to auxiliary contraction without requiring small global factor amplitudes.
attack_outcome.not_completed: The current bounds do not certify a small interaction budget in the beta(a)->infinity regime. They are upper bounds, so their growth does not prove that the actual physical theory fails to mix.
attack_outcome.next_specific_estimate: Replace the growing global-oscillation bound with a scale-uniform bound on the relevant coarse mixed interactions after cancellation of the background action, then prove entry into a physical-scale contraction regime.
attack_outcome.physical_bridge: A valid physical-time locality/clustering or original-transfer slab argument is still required. The color-update theorem is about an auxiliary sampler.
attack_outcome.sources_and_large_fields: Existing exact source transport remains available, but this increment does not establish scale-uniform source estimates or absorb large-field/boundary tails into the mixing budget.

remaining: Derive a small weighted interaction budget for the actual renormalized Wilson trajectory at a fixed physical scale, with a uniformly bounded admissible coloring or a method that handles weighted long-range interactions.
Improve the conservative global-oscillation bounds by controlling mixed interactions after background cancellation, including large-field and boundary contributions and sourced observables.
Prove physical-time clustering or fixed-physical-slab contraction for the original Wilson transfer; an auxiliary heat-bath contraction alone is not a physical mass-gap theorem.
Construct nontrivial continuum correlations on the same trajectory, including full Schwartz bounds, contact renormalization, reflection positivity and a nonzero finite-energy excitation.
All twelve full Clay obligations remain open.
